newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sells 182-day bills, rate falls.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sells 182-day bills, rate falls.

text.p: Croatia's Finance Ministry said it raised 28.5 million kuna in 182-day treasury bills at an auction on Tuesday.
The amount fell short of its target by 11.5 million kuna on total bids of 36.5 million kuna, it said.
The issue was priced higher at 95.025 from 94.917 last month, with the rate falling 24 basis points to 10.50 percent.
Clients can view full auction details on page MFHT.
Most of the issue went to banks, with the non-banking sector's share amounting to 5.26 percent. Auctions are not open to foreign investors though they can place their bids through Croatian banks.
Bills are payable in two days and mature on January 15, 1998.

The Ministry announced the next auction for July 29, when 100 million kuna worth of 91-day bills will be offered. They were last issued at 10.15 percent interest in late June. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
